scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

First, the situation: The person is a 26-year-old man who took his dad's business idea, got IP rights, and started a successful business. The dad is upset, feeling betrayed, and called the son an asshole. The mom and granddad support the son, but the sister is defending the dad. The son offered the dad 20% of profits, which was rejected. So, the question is: Is the son being unreasonable, or is he justified in taking the idea and running with it? Let me think about the dad's perspective. He came up with the idea, which he probably thought was genius. But he didn't act on it, maybe because he's more introverted and struggles to get things done. The son saw the potential and took action, which led to success. From the dad's viewpoint, it might feel like his idea was stolen, especially since he didn't get any credit or financial gain from it. On the other hand, the son's perspective is that he recognized the idea's potential and had the drive to make it successful. He might feel that he's the one who deserves the credit and profits because he was the one who put in the work to turn the idea into a business. He also mentioned that his dad has always been good with ideas but not with execution, so he took the initiative. I wonder about the dynamics between the son and dad. The son says they're complete opposites. The dad is introverted and intelligent but lacks action, while the son is more impulsive and gets things done. The son feels more like his granddad, which might mean he's more traditional or masculine in his approach. The son offered 20% of profits, which is a significant offer, but the dad rejected it. That suggests the dad's hurt and betrayal run deeper than just financial compensation. It's more about the principle of the idea being taken without his consent. I also think about the mom and sister's reactions. The mom supports the son, which might indicate that she sees his actions as responsible and necessary. The sister, however, is defending the dad, which could mean she's more empathetic towards his feelings of being overlooked or undervalued. In terms of whether the son is AITA, I need to consider if he acted unreasonably. He took the idea without discussing it with his dad first, which could be seen as disrespectful. However, he also saw the potential and acted on it, which led to success. The offer of 20% shows he's willing to share the profits, but the dad's refusal indicates that the issue is more about recognition and betrayal. I think the key points are: 1. Did the son steal the idea without permission? It seems like he took it without discussing it, which could be seen as stealing. 2. Did he acknowledge his dad's contribution? He offered a financial share but maybe didn't give enough credit or emotional acknowledgment. 3. How would a reasonable person handle this situation? Perhaps by discussing the idea with the dad first, getting his permission, and ensuring he felt valued. So, considering all this, I think the son might be AITA because he didn't respect his dad's ownership of the idea and didn't handle the situation in a way that acknowledged his dad's feelings and contributions beyond just the financial aspect.
